youtube.baslik: How can an ear with no hearing respond in a hearing test? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: A loud test tone can cross through the skull to the opposite cochlea; this is called cross-hearing. If it goes unnoticed, an ear with no hearing can be recorded as having a moderate loss; to prevent this, masking noise is given to the other ear.

bilgiler: A loud test tone can cross the skull to the other cochlea: cross-hearing.
An ear with no hearing can look like a moderate loss.
To prevent this, noise goes to the other ear: clinical masking.

cumleler: How can an ear with no hearing respond in a test?
A loud test tone also vibrates the skull through the earphone.
The vibration reaches the opposite cochlea, and is heard there.
So an ear with no hearing can look like a moderate loss.
To prevent this, noise goes to the other ear: clinical masking.
